The move joins both halves of the motion by accepting Jesus’s transformative influence while arguing that meaningful dignity, obligation, and moral distinctions require objective grounding.
Ehrman argues that universal concern for needy strangers is historically recent and therefore should not be claimed as an objective moral value.

McDowell accepts the Christian origin of a universal charitable ethic, grounds human dignity in God’s image, and argues that subjectivism cannot explain why charitable giving is better than harmful causes.
